cases.description: Two anchor elements at the start of one paragraph are a structural error, attached to the $body that holds the block (§6.2, decisions I1.1 and I1.6).
The same at the start of a list item in a section, attached to that section's $body.

A block anchor may start a list item at any depth and any paragraph outside block quotes, a list item's second paragraph included, so neither <a id> here is plain HTML and nothing is reported (§6.2, decision T, which widened I1.7).
A tag repeated in a data $tags array is stored data and stays as written (§6.2, decision I1.5).
Each repeat after the first gets one duplicate-tag warning, at the node that holds the array: one for open at the root and one for a at /item (§6.2, Appendix D, decision I1.5).

A list item inside a block quote carries no block anchor, since block quotes stay prose and "at any depth" means list nesting; its <a id> is plain HTML with anchor-element-ignored (§6.2, decision J2).

Block anchors start a list item, a list item's second paragraph and a nested list item; each range is its CommonMark block without trailing white space, so the first item's three trailing spaces are not in it (§5.9, §6.2, decisions P10 and T).
An anchor element with a class at the start of a block is a validation error, block-anchor-class, so the record stays readable (§6.2, decision P5).
Character references in an anchor element's attributes are not decoded, so id="aab" is the name aab, which is anchor-invalid, where decoding would give the valid name aab (§6.2, decision P8).
A tag that is not a valid name and is repeated gives one anchor-invalid per occurrence, besides the duplicate-tag warning for the repeat (Appendix D, decision Q3).
